name: Mulethi
kitchenUse: A small piece of root chewed or simmered in tea for a sore throat, for a few days only.

typicalUse.adultAmount: 2–4 g of powder a day, for short periods
typicalUse.note: Long or heavy use is unsafe because of glycyrrhizin. Deglycyrrhizinated licorice (DGL) products remove it.

cautions.note: Raises blood pressure and lowers potassium with regular use. Even small amounts have caused serious problems in people with high blood pressure or a salty diet. Avoid.
Large or long use can cause an irregular heartbeat and, rarely, cardiac arrest. Avoid with heart disease.
Avoid in pregnancy; large amounts are linked to earlier delivery.
Little is known about safety while breastfeeding; avoid.

interactions.effect: Can cause dangerously low potassium with water pills.
Increases steroid effects and side effects.
Low potassium raises the risk with digoxin.

evidence.summary: Its side effects (high blood pressure, low potassium, heart rhythm problems) are well documented in humans. Evidence for benefits is limited; a licorice gargle may ease sore throat after surgery.
